text: “Yes, madame,” replied the magistrate. “Then you pity me!” “Sincerely, madame.” “And you understand what brings me here?” “You wish to speak to me about the circumstance which has just happened?” “Yes, sir,—a fearful misfortune.” “You mean a mischance.” “A mischance?” repeated the baroness. “Alas, madame,” said the procureur with his imperturbable calmness of manner, “I consider those alone misfortunes which are irreparable.” “And do you suppose this will be forgotten?” “Everything will be forgotten, madame,” said Villefort. “Your daughter will be married tomorrow, if not today—in a week, if not tomorrow; and I do not think you can regret the intended husband of your daughter.” Madame Danglars gazed on Villefort, stupefied to find him so almost insultingly calm. “Am I come to a friend?” she asked in a tone full of mournful dignity.
